title: Strict systems and the unchanged left-extension interface
statement:
For a sheaf-ring sequence B on a site, define a strict system as B_n-module sheaves M_n with actual restriction-scalar transitions for every m≤n, satisfying identity and composition on sections. Morphisms are componentwise linear maps commuting with transitions. Construct its category, componentwise abelian structure and colimits, exact additive evaluation and exact subsequence restriction, derived evaluations and restrictions, next-selected indices and their composition identity. Define the unchanged predicates for flat-term independent K-flat representatives, normalized ordinary-derived left extension data, tensor coherence, and the full SystemLevelLeftExtensionTheory interface. All old public definition and structure signatures are retained.

      ((derivedSystemEvaluation (selectedSystemRings B r) (systemNextSelected r (m + 1))).obj N) ≫

        ((transition (selectedSystemRings B r) (systemNextSelected_mono r m)).app N)) ≫
    (selectedDerivedBelow B r m).inv.app N

    (systemSubsequence (selectedSystemRings B r) s).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app

    (f : (selected B r).derived.obj ((selected (selectedSystemRings B r) s).derived.obj P) ⟶ M),

proof.text: The category laws hold componentwise. Kernels are computed on sections; cokernels and arbitrary small colimits are obtained by componentwise sheaf-module colimits, with transition maps induced by their universal properties. The resulting abelian structure and evaluation exactness agree with the original normalized structures. A map and a zero object are detected by their components. Strictly increasing natural-number embeddings are unbounded, so minimum selected indices exist; minimality proves monotonicity and composition of these indices. The remaining structures are explicit records of the same normalized adjunction and tensor statements.
